Solve \(h(x)=\cos x-2x=0\) numerically with Newton's method: \(x_{n+1}=x_n-\frac{\cos x_n-2x_n}{-\sin x_n-2}\). Starting at \(x_0=0.45\) gives \(x\approx0.4501836\), which rounds to \(0.4502\).

Thus the right extreme is \(x=2\left(\frac32\right)\frac{\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\), the circle's radius.
